question: Which HTML element represents the top-level (largest) heading of a page section?
options: <h1>|<h6>|<head>|<header>
explanation: <h1> is the highest-level heading. <h6> is the smallest, <head> holds page metadata and <header> is a sectioning container.

question: Which attribute gives an image alternative text for screen readers and for when the image fails to load?
options: alt|title|src|href
explanation: The alt attribute is the text alternative of an . src is the file location, href is for links.

question: Which element is the most appropriate for a block of main navigation links?
options: <section>|<menu>|<nav>|<div class="nav">
explanation: <nav> is the semantic landmark for major navigation; screen readers can jump straight to it.

question: What does the for attribute of a <label> do?
options: Sets the font used by the label|Links the label to the form control whose id has the same value|Names the field that is sent to the server|Marks the field as required
explanation: label for="x" connects to the control with id="x", so clicking the label focuses the control and assistive technology reads it.

question: Which statement about the defer and async attributes of <script> is correct?
options: async guarantees execution order; defer does not|defer runs scripts in order after the document is parsed; async runs each script as soon as it downloads, in no guaranteed order|Both pause HTML parsing until the script has finished running|defer only works for inline scripts
explanation: Both download in parallel with parsing. defer preserves order and waits for the parse to finish; async executes immediately on arrival.

question: Which CSS property changes the colour of text?
options: font-color|color|text-color|foreground
explanation: color sets the foreground (text) colour. The other names are not valid CSS properties.

question: Which selector targets every element that has the class "card"?
options: .card|#card|card|*card
explanation: A dot selects by class. # selects by id, and a bare name selects an element type.

question: In the CSS box model, what is the order of the layers from the inside to the outside?
options: content, padding, border, margin|content, border, padding, margin|margin, border, padding, content|padding, content, margin, border
explanation: Content sits in the middle, then padding, then the border, and margin is the outermost space.

question: Which declaration turns an element into a flex container for one-dimensional layout of its children?
options: display: block|display: inline|position: flex|display: flex
explanation: display: flex enables the flexbox layout model on the element's children.

question: Rule 1 ".a .b { color: red; }" appears before rule 2 ".b.c { color: blue; }". A <span class="b c"> sits inside <div class="a">. What colour is the span's text?
options: Blue|Red|Black (the default colour)|Neither; the CSS is invalid
explanation: Both selectors have the same specificity (two classes). When specificity ties, the rule declared later wins, so blue.

question: Which keyword declares a block-scoped variable that can be reassigned?
options: let|const|static|final
explanation: let is block-scoped and reassignable. const cannot be reassigned. static and final are not JavaScript variable keywords.

question: What does typeof "hello" evaluate to?
options: "string"|"text"|"char"|"word"
explanation: JavaScript has a single string type; typeof returns the string "string".

question: Which array method returns a NEW array containing only the elements that pass a test?
options: map|filter|forEach|reduce
explanation: filter keeps elements for which the callback returns true. map transforms every element, forEach returns nothing, reduce collapses to one value.

question: How does === differ from == in JavaScript?
options: === assigns a value; == compares|=== compares value and type without type coercion; == converts types before comparing|=== compares only object references|They behave identically
explanation: Strict equality (===) never coerces, so 5 === "5" is false while 5 == "5" is true.

question: What is logged by: for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++) { setTimeout(() => console.log(i), 0); }
explanation: var is function-scoped, so all callbacks share one i. They run after the loop ends, when i is 3. Using let would log 0 1 2.

question: Which meta tag is essential so a page scales correctly on mobile browsers?
options: <meta charset="utf-8">|<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">|<meta name="responsive" content="true">|<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="30">
explanation: The viewport meta tag tells mobile browsers to use the device width instead of a zoomed-out desktop width.

question: Which CSS at-rule applies styles only when a condition such as screen width is met?
options: @import|@keyframes|@font-face|@media
explanation: @media defines media queries. @import loads a stylesheet, @keyframes defines animations, @font-face loads fonts.

question: Which CSS unit is relative to the width of the viewport?
options: px|vw|pt|em
explanation: 1vw equals 1% of the viewport width. px and pt are absolute units; em is relative to font size.

question: What does a mobile-first approach mean?
options: Design only for phones and ignore desktops|Write desktop styles first and shrink them with max-width queries|Hide all content on large screens|Write base styles for small screens, then enhance for larger screens with min-width media queries
explanation: Mobile-first starts with the smallest layout and adds complexity as space increases.

question: Which declaration creates as many columns of at least 200px as fit in the row and stretches them to fill it?
options: grid-template-columns: 200px 200px;|grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 200px);|grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr));|grid-auto-flow: column 200px;
explanation: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr)) lets the grid decide how many columns fit while each is at least 200px.

question: Which command creates a local copy of an existing remote repository?
options: git clone|git init|git commit|git branch
explanation: git clone downloads the repository and its history. git init creates a brand-new empty repository.

question: Which command records the staged changes as a new commit with a message?
options: git add -m "message"|git commit -m "message"|git push -m "message"|git save "message"
explanation: git commit -m creates the commit. git add stages files; git push uploads commits.

question: What does git add . do?
options: Commits all changes immediately|Uploads the files to GitHub|Deletes untracked files|Stages new and modified files in the current directory for the next commit
explanation: Staging prepares changes for a commit; it does not commit or upload anything.

question: Two teammates edit the same line of a file on different branches and you merge them. What happens?
options: Git silently keeps the newer commit|Git deletes one of the branches|Git reports a merge conflict; you edit the file to resolve it and then commit|The merge succeeds and keeps both versions automatically
explanation: Git cannot decide which edit is correct, so it marks the conflict and waits for a human to resolve it.

question: What is the difference between git fetch and git pull?
options: pull only downloads; fetch merges and pushes|They are exactly the same command|fetch downloads remote changes without merging them; pull is a fetch followed by a merge into the current branch|fetch uploads local commits; pull deletes them
explanation: fetch is the safe look-before-you-merge step. pull = fetch + merge (or rebase).

question: What is a React component?
options: A database table|A reusable piece of UI, usually a function that returns JSX|A CSS file|A server route
explanation: Components are the building blocks of a React interface.

question: What does JSX stand for?
options: Java Syntax Extension|JavaScript XML, a syntax extension that looks like HTML|JSON Exchange|JavaScript Extra
explanation: JSX lets you write markup inside JavaScript; tools compile it into normal JavaScript calls.

question: Which hook adds local state to a function component?
options: useEffect|useRef|useState|useContext
explanation: useState returns the current value and a setter. useEffect is for side effects.

question: How does a parent component pass data down to a child component?
options: Through props|Through a global variable only|By calling useState inside the child|Through CSS variables
explanation: Props are the inputs of a component and flow from parent to child.

question: When does useEffect(() => { ... }, []) with an empty dependency array run?
options: Once, after the first render (mount)|After every render|Only when the component unmounts|Never
explanation: An empty dependency array means there is nothing to re-trigger it, so it runs once after mounting.
